meta.personalization: S163 closed the RUM -> perf-budget loop and produced the first concrete ambient split shortlist. This audit deliberately avoids another broad platform wishlist and focuses on converting yesterday's evidence into small, compounding runtime and decision-loop upgrades. High-risk flips remain evidence-gated: no Trusted Types enforce without KV soak visibility, no mobile nav default swap without aggregated interaction data.

candidates.title: Lazy-load command-palette.js behind the first search intent instead of parsing it on every page
candidates.why: S163's ambient coverage report named command-palette.js as the largest always-shipped split candidate. Most visitors never press Cmd/Ctrl+K, so parsing the full fuzzy-search and AI-synthesis UI on every route is unnecessary. A tiny loader preserves the feature while turning its cost into intent-paid work.
candidates.recipe: Add `assets/command-palette-loader.js` as the ambient source and remove `assets/command-palette.js` from `AMBIENT_SOURCES`. The loader listens for Cmd/Ctrl+K and the mobile search pill, injects `/assets/command-palette.js` once, and replays the open request after load. Add a build check that fails if the heavy palette returns to the ambient bundle.

candidates.title: Build /api/nav-sheet-stats.json from privacy-minimized RUM ux events
candidates.why: S163 instrumented the bottom-sheet nav but left the founder default-swap waiting for an aggregate that does not exist yet. A committed, public-safe stats file gives the decision a real threshold: opens, close causes, and sample sufficiency without IDs or raw user text.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/build-nav-sheet-stats.mjs` that reads `data/rum-raw.ndjson` or an explicit `--from=` export, counts allowlisted `nav-sheet:*` ux events by route and cause, writes `api/nav-sheet-stats.json`, and supports `--check` + `--self-test`. Wire it into `build` and `build:check`.

candidates.title: Expose whether RUM has enough samples to flip strict perf gates
candidates.why: The site now has a field-first perf gate, but the next action still requires humans to inspect JSON and remember the 50-sample threshold. A tiny readiness artifact turns that threshold into a visible machine-readable signal for /start, /closeout, and future Hub tiles.
candidates.recipe: Extend the RUM summary flow or add a small companion output that records total samples, sufficient routes, and `strictReady` for `/`. Keep it public-safe and wire a check so stale or missing RUM readiness is visible before closeout.

candidates.title: Guard the ambient split so heavy gated modules cannot silently re-enter the critical bundle
candidates.why: The mature-codebase failure mode is not the first split; it is the quiet regression six sessions later. A structural gate that names forbidden heavy sources in the ambient bundle preserves the performance win and keeps future edits honest.
candidates.recipe: Teach `report-ambient-coverage.mjs --check` or a focused verifier to fail when `assets/command-palette.js` appears in `AMBIENT_SOURCES`. The check should allow `assets/command-palette-loader.js` and print the raw KB avoided.
